title: Lada, Memphis Five, Durante and other bands asked about
summary: The interviewer asks about Anton Lada, the Memphis Five, Durante's band, Baquet and the New Orleans Rhythm Kings; Hardy knew them only by record or hearsay.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh, you recall, uh, Lada, Anton Lada. No. He came north, and, uh, his band was reasonably popular, uh, especially for recording purposes, apparently, he was a good entertaining band. And, uh, made, corresponded to the Dukes of Dixieland in his day, entertaining, uh, New Orleans, I think. Um, there was a band in the East, I wondered if you'd ever heard, uh, the Memphis Five.
I think I have heard the Memphis Five, yes. Yeah. Either on a record or someplace or someplace.
Yeah, well, they were popular on records, uh, Phil Napoleon, and something like Miss Maul,
Yeah. And, uh, uh, Jimmy Durante, for a while, had a Dixieland style band. He played the pianist probably.
And, uh, people, New Orleans musicians, such as, uh, Baquet. Baquet, yeah.

Uh, there were, uh, bands in Chicago, uh, prior to 1925, that, uh, were largely New Orleans men, such as the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. Yes, I've heard of them, too. Mm-hmm. You know them by way of record. In, uh, Peoria, there was no New Orleans musicians, to your knowledge? No, not that I knew of.
